compiled_state.author: Joe Oakhart
compiled_state.description:
## Problem

A draft-PR run whose CI needed even one repair never opens its pull request. The work completes, the branch is pushed, CI passes and every review gate passes, then the final step is discarded and the workflow fails.

Observed on pilot ticket `5d28-7811-5391-4bd6` against `archive-massgov-pfml`:

```
action discarded by sequence gate: 5d28-7811-5391-4bd6 sequence 103 not ahead of 105
```

The audit trail shows the run reaching `POLICY_EVALUATED proceed` and `PR_CREATION_AUTHORIZED`, then `side_effect_discarded STALE_REVIEW_DISCARDED` for `github.open_pr` at sequence 103.

## Cause

`PostgresSequenceGate.admit` admits an action only when its sequence exceeds the one the task already holds. The numbers each stage hands out therefore have to rise in the order the stages run.

They do not. `DraftPullRequestWorkflow` runs its stages in this order, with a claim version of 1:

| Order | Stage | Sequence expression | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | commit | `base + _COMMIT_OFFSET` | 102 |
| 2 | repair attempt N | `base + _OPEN_PR_OFFSET + _REPAIR_STRIDE * N` | 105, 107, ... |
| 3 | open PR | `base + _OPEN_PR_OFFSET` | 103 |
| 4 | approval, promote | `base + _CI_TRIGGER_OFFSET + _REPAIR_STRIDE * M + 1 or 2` | 115, 116 |

Repair commits use `_OPEN_PR_OFFSET` as the base of their own band and add a stride on top, so every repair outranks the step that constant is named for. That numbering only holds if the pull request opens before CI repairs it. The workflow opens the pull request after CI and after the review gates, so the first repair leaves `open_pr` permanently behind the gate.

With no repairs the gate sits at 102 from the commit, 103 clears it, and the run succeeds. That is why this went unnoticed. It reproduces whenever CI fails once.

`_promote` already computes a base that clears the repair band. `_open_pull_request` was the only post-repair stage that did not.

## Approach

Give the two post-repair stages one shared definition of where their band starts, so they cannot drift apart again.

- Add `_post_repair_sequence_base`, returning `claim_version * _SEQUENCE_STRIDE + _CI_TRIGGER_OFFSET + _REPAIR_STRIDE * max(max_repair_attempts, attempts_used)`. This is the expression `_promote` already used, lifted to a method.
- Open the pull request at that base. It lands at 114 with the default cap of 5 repair attempts, above the highest possible repair at 113 and below approval at 115.
- Promote from the same base, leaving approval and promote unchanged at 115 and 116.
- Rename `_OPEN_PR_OFFSET` to `_REPAIR_BASE_OFFSET`. After this change the constant seeds only the repair band, and the old name is what invited the collision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_post_repair_sequence_base` returns `claim_version * _SEQUENCE_STRIDE + _CI_TRIGGER_OFFSET + _REPAIR_STRIDE * max(max_repair_attempts, attempts_used)`, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k sequence`
- [ ] A run whose CI needed a repair opens its pull request at sequence 114 for claim version 1, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k full_chain`
- [ ] Every sequence the workflow issues is admitted by `InMemorySequenceGate` when replayed in stage execution order, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k clears_the_gate`
- [ ] The approval sequence stays at 115 for claim version 1, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k promote`
- [ ] The promotion sequence stays at 116 for claim version 1, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k promote`
- [ ] `_OPEN_PR_OFFSET` no longer appears in the codebase, checked by `rg -n _OPEN_PR_OFFSET services tests`

## Testing

New test `test_every_sequenced_action_clears_the_gate_when_ci_needed_a_repair` drives the repair scenario, then replays the commit, open_pr, approval, promote sequences through the production `InMemorySequenceGate` in execution order. Against the unfixed code it reports `[('github.open_pr', 103, 105)]`, an exact match for the production discard record.

Commands:

- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py tests/unit/test_coordination_sequencing.py`
- `.venv/bin/ruff check services tests`
- `.venv/bin/pytest` for the full suite

file_impact.reason: Add _post_repair_sequence_base, open the PR from it, promote from it, and rename _OPEN_PR_OFFSET to _REPAIR_BASE_OFFSET
Add a gate replay test proving every sequence is admitted when CI needed a repair, and update the two assertions that pinned the old open_pr number
